info.name: 09 · Reviews — annotator verdict workflow
info.description:
The reviewer loop — a red-teamer's flagged submission is assigned to an **annotator**, who reads it and records a verdict (`approved`/`rejected`). Two actors: **admin** (orchestrates + authors the flag on its own conversation) and the seeded **annotator** (the reviewer).

**Flow.** A) admin builds the tree — model → group → **approve** → evaluation → assign → conversation group → send a message (SSE, no key needed — the user message persists) → flag it; B) admin assigns the annotator, who sees it in the queue, reads the submission + transcript, and records the verdict, then admin confirms; C) re-assigning the same reviewer is **409**; D) the queue + picker + **bulk** paths — `GET /reviews/{id}`, `GET /review-queue` (before and after the required count is met), `GET /submissions/{id}/assignable-reviewers` (the assign picker) and `POST /reviews/bulk` with a partial-success row.

**Auth model.** Per-request: `{{admin_token}}` orchestrates, `{{annotator_token}}` reviews. Self-contained — no `00-bootstrap`, **no manual token** (uses the seeded `annotator@test.com`, so no register/verify/elevate), no live model key.

**Contract notes.** A fresh group is `pending_approval` — evaluations 409 until approved. The message endpoint streams SSE; without a credential the assistant turn errors but the flagged **user** message is `complete`. Flag-create is owner-only (admin authors); the reviewer must differ from the author and be an assignable annotator (a global annotator, for this public group).

**Leftovers.** The evaluation group leaks (no group DELETE; `run_suffix`-unique); the seeded annotator is left intact. Everything else is torn down.

**Verified:** 58/58 checks green end-to-end against a live stack (`make up` + `make seedlocal`).

request.description: Authenticate the seeded admin (orchestrates + authors the flag). Sets `run_suffix` and a fresh UUID `client_msg_id`.

item.name: 2 · Log in as the seeded annotator (reviewer)

request.description: Authenticate the seeded `annotator` — holds the global `annotator` role (`reviews:*`) and is an assignable reviewer for a public group. Using the seed identity removes the emailed-verify-token step entirely.
Resolve the annotator's user id (admin, `users:read`) — needed as `reviewer_id` on assignment.

item.name: 4 · Log in as red teamer (holds reviews:read only)

request.description: `red_teamer` holds `reviews:read` but **not** `reviews:create` — the identity folder D needs to prove the assign picker is gated, not merely that it works for an admin.

item.name: A · Admin builds a flagged submission

request.description: A model to assign — no credential needed for this flow (the flagged **user** message persists regardless).

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Review engagement {{run_suffix}}",
  "description": "Public so the global annotator is assignable.",
  "access_level": "public",
  "start_date": "2026-09-01",
  "allowed_model_ids": ["{{rv_model_id}}"]
}

request.description: **Public** — the assignable-reviewer pool for a public group is every global `annotator` holder (our reviewer).
Evaluations can be added only to an **approved/published** group; the owner may approve their own. Without this, the next step 409s.
The evaluation the submission belongs to.
Capture the assignment id for the conversation group.
Every conversation (group) targets exactly one scenario — the create posts to `/scenarios/{scenario_id}/...`. Default `required_reviews` (1) keeps the review-queue math of this scenario unchanged.

item.name: 6 · Create a conversation group (+ its conversation)

request.description: A conversation belongs to a conversation group — this creates the group plus one conversation per `models` entry. Captures the embedded conversation id.

Persist a user turn to flag. The endpoint streams SSE; with no model credential the assistant turn finalizes to `error` but the **user** message is `complete` and flaggable — so this returns 200 and needs no key.

exec: pm.test('→ 200 (user message persists regardless of model key)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

request.description: Capture the user message id to flag.

exec: pm.test('a live user message exists', () => pm.expect(user, 'user message').to.be.an('object'));

request.description: The flag IS the submission a reviewer is assigned to. Flag-create is owner-only, so admin (the conversation owner) authors it; the reviewer differs from the author (no self-review).
Create a `pending` review assigning the annotator (requires `reviews:create`; the reviewer must be an assignable annotator for this public group and not the author).

item.name: 2 · Annotator sees the review in its queue

request.description: The annotator lists reviews assigned to it.

exec: pm.test('assigned review is listed', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().items.some(r => r.id === pm.collectionVariables.get('rv_review_id'))).to.be.true);

request.description: The reviewer's detail view: the flag + flagged messages + reviews so far.
Full parent-conversation transcript for context (the owner-scoped history endpoint is unavailable to a non-owner reviewer).

body.raw:
{
  "status": "approved",
  "successful_exploit": true,
  "unique_exploit": false,
  "valid_submission": true,
  "number_prompts": 2,
  "notes": "Reproduced; clear policy violation."
}

request.description: Record the verdict, moving the review `pending → approved`. Only the assigned reviewer (or a break-glass manager) may do this.

item.name: 6 · Admin confirms the verdict on the flag

request.description: Filter reviews by the submission — the recorded verdict is visible to the orchestrator.

exec: pm.test('verdict visible to admin', () => pm.expect(r && r.status).to.eql('approved'));

request.description: Assigning the same reviewer twice (or to an already-decided submission) is a 409.

item.name: D · Queue, picker & bulk assign

exec: pm.test('carries the verdict folder B recorded', () => pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('approved'));
pm.test('and the reviewer it belongs to', () => pm.expect(b.reviewer_id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('rv_annotator_id')));

request.description: `reviews:read`. The single-review read the console uses when opening one assignment; the list endpoint in folder B is the queue view.

item.name: 2 · Review queue no longer holds the satisfied flag

request.description: The queue lists flags whose **completed** verdicts fall short of the scenario's `required_reviews` (fallback 1 when the flag targets no live scenario). Folder B recorded the only verdict this flag needed, so it is done — that absence is the assertion.

item.name: 3 · Admin flags a second message (a fresh submission)

request.description: Flag create is **owner-only** — no break-glass — so the author must be whoever owns the conversation, which here is the admin who built it in folder A. A conversation can carry many independent flags.

**FE note:** this backs the assign-reviewer picker. It returns exactly what `POST /reviews` accepts — the group's assignable-reviewer pool minus the flag's author and anyone already assigned — so the picker and the assign gate can never disagree. Gated on `reviews:create`, like the assign it feeds. The group is `public`, so the pool is every global `reviews:annotate` holder.

item.name: 5 · Red teamer cannot open the picker → 403

request.description: The picker is gated on **`reviews:create`** — the same permission as the assign it feeds — so a red teamer, who may read reviews of its own flags, cannot enumerate assignable reviewers. Without this row the endpoint was only ever seen succeeding for an admin, and a regression that dropped its gate would leak the group's reviewer pool to every participant.

exec: pm.test('partial success: 1 ok, 1 failed', () => { pm.expect(b.succeeded).to.eql(1); pm.expect(b.failed).to.eql(1); });
pm.test('the duplicate pair is a per-row 409', () => pm.expect(dup.error.status).to.eql(409));

request.description: Assigning many reviewers to many flags in one call, via the platform `BulkRequest` envelope. Each row gets its own savepoint, so the duplicate `(flag, reviewer)` pair fails **alone** (the partial-unique index is the arbiter) while the good row still commits.

item.name: 7 · The fresh submission is in the queue

exec: pm.test('with an assigned but unfinished review', () => { pm.expect(row.completed_reviews).to.eql(0); pm.expect(row.required_reviews).to.be.above(0); });
pm.test('and the pending review is embedded', () => pm.expect(row.reviews.map(r => r.status)).to.include('pending'));

request.description: The same queue as step 2, now with a flag that genuinely needs work — the pair proves the completed-vs-required rule in both directions.

exec: pm.test('reported as a dry run', () => pm.expect(b.dry_run).to.eql(true));
pm.test('the duplicate still reports as it would fail', () => pm.expect(b.failed).to.eql(1));

request.description: `dry_run` rolls the whole envelope back instead of committing — the console's "preview" for a batch assign. The row still reports the 409 it *would* hit.
Self-cleanup: this folder's own fixtures go before the shared Teardown runs.
Children before parents — the review above is already gone.

item.description: The reviewer-facing read side (`GET /reviews/{id}`, `GET /review-queue`), the assign picker (`GET /submissions/{id}/assignable-reviewers`) and the many-to-many bulk assign (`POST /reviews/bulk`). Self-cleaning, so it slots in ahead of the shared Teardown.

request.description: A decided review can be removed by its reviewer or a break-glass manager (admin).
Soft-delete the submission.
Soft-delete the conversation (its empty group is reaped).
Delete the evaluation (cascades the assignment).
Soft-delete the model (no credential was set). The seeded annotator is left intact; the evaluation group leaks (no group DELETE).
